title: Derivatives: concept and purpose
objectives: Define a derivative and list its three uses.
body_md:
A **derivative** is a contract whose value **derives from an underlying** such as a stock, an index, a commodity, a currency or an interest rate.

## Uses

1. **Hedging:** reduce risk on an existing position.
2. **Speculation:** take a view with leverage.
3. **Arbitrage:** lock in a riskless profit from mispricing.

## Forwards vs futures

| Feature | Forward | Future |
|---|---|---|
| Trading | OTC, customised | Exchange traded, standardised |
| Counterparty risk | Yes | Removed by the clearing corporation |
| Settlement | At maturity | Daily mark-to-market, then final settlement |
| Liquidity | Low | High |

## Participants

**Hedgers**, **speculators**, **arbitrageurs**, plus market makers and clearing members.

## Why leverage matters

A small margin controls a large exposure, so both gains and losses are magnified.

> **Exam tip:** Futures are exchange-traded forwards with daily settlement.
example: A farmer sells wheat forward to lock a price. A fund buys index futures to hedge a portfolio. A trader buys a stock future to bet on a rise.
say: Derivatives can hedge or speculate; the leverage cuts both ways.
Exchange-traded contracts are guaranteed by the clearing corporation.
never: Futures are risk free because they are on an exchange.
A small margin means a small risk.
